openings.claim: Shift sideways restraint from seal friction to removable locating bolts on two padded strip saddles; separate balanced hold-down may avoid opposite-corner lift. Drill only strips; upper/lower rim saddles use four bolts/four pads, remaining two bolts locate hatch edges along pull; cord tethers recoverable parts. Release/move saddles entirely outside marked opening.
openings.discriminator: Locators predict less displacement without extra corner compression; rival straps increase normal force, making restraint compression-dependent. Hypothesized loop: friction restraint causes demand for extra tightening after slip; demand causes technician left-corner tightening; response alters restraint through opposite-corner lift/reduced contact. Only tightening-to-lift is supplied; other arrows/friction effect are hypotheses. Remove slip-triggered tightening through preset balanced closure; sham retains return rule. No return influence if displacement/lift differences stay within ruler resolution; invalid sham leaves loop unresolved. Defeat: saddle movement, locator clearance >1 mm, disturbed rocking, reopening >30 seconds, seal damage.
openings.probe: Before fabrication confirm underside access, locator reach, reversible pad seating, full opening clearance. Within twelve closure/pull trials, ten candidate cycles include final right-contact 1 mm card disturbance; measure marked position, 20 N displacement, reopening time, visible seal condition. Reserve two disturbed feedback-comparison trials with equal initial closure setting/20 N demand; comparison counts only if return response varies safely/measurably.
openings.uncertainty: Attachment capacity/success unprovided. Rim access, strip/bolt geometry, cord anchorage, clamp capacity are indispensable unknowns; supplied strips may not form saddles within ninety minutes. Pull-direction locators do not establish other-direction repeatability.

lineage.reason: Causal, rival, feedback, defeat, resource and uncertainty conditions retained; fit remains uncertain.

decision: Feasibility/discrimination probe only. Retain hatch/rim/seal; no drilling/cutting/gluing/permanent deformation, powered mechanism, lost loose parts or blocked opening. Ninety-minute fabrication/twenty-minute observation limits hold. Ten-cycle success requires marked position within 1 mm, 20 N resistance, one-technician reopening within 30 seconds, no new visible seal tears; disturbed closure waives only contact continuity. Unknown geometry precludes deployment.
